newsitem.title: USA: Investors hold back on bullion coins in March 1997.
newsitem.headline: Investors hold back on bullion coins in March 1997.

text.p: U.S. investors held back on purchasing gold and silver bullion coins in March, after buying large amounts of the precious metal coins in the first two months of the year, industry consultants CPM Group said.
"Investors may be waiting for prices in both metals to move higher before they return to these coins in full force," CPM Group managing director, Jeffrey Christian said.
In March 51,500 ounces of American Eagle gold coins were sold, a 17.6 percent decrease from 62,500 ounces in February, but up 25.2 percent from March 1996.
But investors had bought a total of 113,750 ounces of American Eagles in the first two months of the year, up on only 25,500 ounces in the first two months of 1996.
In the first quarter 1997 a total of 165,250 ounces of American Eagle gold coins were sold, up 30 percent on 126,750 ounces in the first quarter last year.
Investors also bought 150,000 ounces of American Eagle silver coins in March 1997, down 61 percent on February's total of 385,000 and down 63.7 percent on 413,000 ounces in March 1996.
But in the first quarter 1997, 970,000 ounces of American Eagle silver coins were sold, up 87.3 percent from 518,000 ounces sold in the first quarter 1996, CPM Group said.
